reason: The cited evidence shows corrosion resistance in AlCrTiV0.5Cux (E1), potential for strength-ductility-corrosion balance in AlTiVNb films (E2), and design strategies for high specific strength in refractory HEAs (E3), but none directly demonstrates the full suite of low density, high strength, corrosion resistance, and high-temperature oxidation resistance via the proposed lattice-distortion/sluggish-diffusion mechanism, nor do they confirm the single-phase or near-amorphous structure in bulk alloys under the specified conditions.
premises: Single-phase or near-amorphous highly disordered solid solution can be achieved in lightweight HEAs by compositional tuning with light elements
Enhanced lattice distortion and sluggish diffusion in such microstructures impede dislocation motion and oxygen/ion diffusion
These features promote formation of stable, protective surface oxide films
Lightweight HEAs with such microstructures can simultaneously achieve low density, high strength, corrosion resistance, and oxidation resistance
The cited evidence directly demonstrates this combination of properties in specific lightweight HEA systems
